review_notes: I read all of Cyclicity.lean and the simp interface in Trace/Basic.lean. Basic has two @[simp] lemmas, traceOfFiniteProjective_dualTensorHom and traceOfFiniteProjective_smulRight. Both rewrite toward simpler normal forms (contractLeft, or evaluation φ x), and their left-hand sides don't overlap. Cyclicity.lean has no simp attributes. The proofs use `simp only` with explicit lemma lists, so they don't depend on the default simp set. I did not recommend @[simp] on traceOfFiniteProjective_comp_comm, because the statement is symmetric under swapping f and g, so it could loop or rewrite unpredictably, and it has no canonical orientation. The commutator lemma has a specific shape (`f.comp g - g.comp f`). I found no use in the supplied sources that would justify making it simp, and the rubric warns against that. I saw no competing rules, unwanted expansion or credible cycles. Remaining uncertainty: I did not search the whole project for downstream uses. I also can't run Lean, so I have no experimental simp behaviour to report.
